embeds.title: 🟡 FBI Warns of Kali365 Phishing-as-a-Service Platform Targeting Microsoft 365
embeds.description:
The FBI issued a public service announcement warning about Kali365, a phishing-as-a-service platform that retrieves Microsoft 365 access tokens by bypassing multi-factor authentication through OAuth device code phishing. The platform, distributed primarily on Telegram as of April, charges affiliates $250 for 30 days or $2,000 annually and provides AI-generated phishing lures, automated campaign templates, tracking dashboards, and token capture capabilities. Researchers at Proofpoint and Arctic Wolf Labs have observed rapid growth in device-code phishing activity since February, with the platform enabling less-technical attackers to conduct campaigns that grant cybercriminal-controlled applications persistent access to Microsoft 365 accounts for data theft, fraud, extortion, and ransomware attacks.
**Sources:** CyberScoop • 🔴 1 corroborating
**CVEs:** none • **Access:** Phishing lures impersonating common enterprise services using OAuth device code authorization
**Incident date:** unknown • **Confidence:** reported
[Read source](https://cyberscoop.com/fbi-phishing-kali365-microsoft365-access-tokens/)
